Exercise: Sit-Up

Category:
strength

Exercise Type:
isolation

Force Type:
pull

Difficulty Level:
beginner

Movement Patterns:

- flexion
- extension_of_the_spine

Primary Muscles:

- abdominals

Secondary Muscles:
None

Equipment:

- bodyweight

Fatigue Score:
2

Systemic Fatigue:
low

Stimulus To Fatigue Ratio:
0.8

Energy Requirement:
moderate

Recovery Time:
1 hours

Goals:

- core_strength_and_stability
- abdominal_muscle_definition

Contraindications:

- Lower back pain
- Recent abdominal surgery

Exercise Variations:

- name: Hanging Sit-Up, equipment: bar or pull-up bar
- name: Ball Sit-Up, equipment: balance ball

Substitution Options:

- exercise_name: Bicycle Crunches, equipment: body only
- exercise_name: Reverse Crunches, equipment: body only

Instructions:

- Lie down on the floor placing your feet either under something that will not move or by having a partner hold them. Your legs should be bent at the knees.
- Place your hands behind your head and lock them together by clasping your fingers. This is the starting position.
- Elevate your upper body so that it creates an imaginary V-shape with your thighs. Breathe out when performing this part of the exercise.
- Once you feel the contraction for a second, lower your upper body back down to the starting position while inhaling.
- Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
